name: unicornscan
summary: A new information gathering and correlation engine.
highlights: -b — *set broken crc sums on [T]ransport layer, [N]etwork layer, or both[TN]
-B — *set source port? or whatever the scan module expects as a number
-d — *set delay type (numeric value, valid options are `1:tsc 2:gtod 3:sleep')
-D — no default Payload, only probe known protocols
-e — *enable modules listed as arguments (output and report currently)
-E — for processing `non-open' responses (icmp errors, tcp rsts...)
-G — *payload group (numeric) for tcp/udp type payload selection (default all)
-H — resolve hostnames during the reporting phase

flags.name: --broken-crc
flags.description: *set broken crc sums on [T]ransport layer, [N]etwork layer, or both[TN]

flags.name: --source-port
flags.description: *set source port? or whatever the scan module expects as a number

flags.name: --delay-type
flags.description: *set delay type (numeric value, valid options are `1:tsc 2:gtod 3:sleep')

flags.name: --no-defpayload
flags.description: no default Payload, only probe known protocols

flags.name: --enable-module
flags.description: *enable modules listed as arguments (output and report currently)

flags.name: --proc-errors
flags.description: for processing `non-open' responses (icmp errors, tcp rsts...)

flags.name: --payload-group
flags.description: *payload group (numeric) for tcp/udp type payload selection (default all)

flags.name: --help
flags.description: help

flags.name: --do-dns
flags.description: resolve hostnames during the reporting phase

flags.name: --interface
flags.description: *interface name, like eth0 or fxp1, not normally required

flags.name: --immediate
flags.description: immediate mode, display things as we find them

flags.name: --ignore-seq
flags.description: *ignore `A'll, 'R'eset sequence numbers for tcp header validation

flags.name: --logfile
flags.description: *write to this file not my terminal

flags.name: --mode
flags.description: *scan mode, tcp (syn) scan is default, U for udp T for tcp `sf' for tcp connect scan and A for arp for -mT you can also specify tcp flags following the T like -mTsFpU for example that would send tcp syn packets with (NO Syn|FIN|NO Push|URG)

flags.name: --module-dir
flags.description: *directory modules are found at (defaults to /usr/lib/unicornscan/modules)

flags.name: --format
flags.description: *format of what to display for replies, see man page for format specification

flags.name: --ports
flags.description: global ports to scan, if not specified in target options

flags.name: --pcap-filter
flags.description: *extra pcap filter string for reciever

flags.name: --covertness
flags.description: *covertness value from 0 to 255

flags.name: --quiet
flags.description: dont use output to screen, its going somewhere else (a database say...)

flags.name: --pps
flags.description: *packets per second (total, not per host, and as you go higher it gets less accurate)

flags.name: --repeats
flags.description: *repeat packet scan N times

flags.name: --source-addr
flags.description: *source address for packets `r' for random

flags.name: --no-shuffle
flags.description: do not shuffle ports

flags.name: --ip-ttl
flags.description: *set TTL on sent packets as in 62 or 6-16 or r64-128

flags.name: --ip-tos
flags.description: *set TOS on sent packets

flags.name: --debug
flags.description: *debug mask

flags.name: --no-openclosed
flags.description: dont say open or closed

flags.name: --safefile
flags.description: *write pcap file of recieved packets

flags.name: --fingerprint
flags.description: *OS fingerprint 0=cisco(def) 1=openbsd 2=WindowsXP 3=p0fsendsyn 4=FreeBSD 5=nmap 6=linux 7:strangetcp

flags.name: --verbose
flags.description: verbose (each time more verbose so -vvvvv is really verbose)

flags.name: --version
flags.description: display version

flags.name: --sniff
flags.description: sniff alike

flags.name: --drone-str
flags.description: *drone String
